column1: 22238§marble§ˈmɑːbl§n. 大理石；（玻璃）弹珠；[pl.] 弹球游戏§In this game, you can insert a marble into a small hole to open the door.§在这个游戏中，你可以往一个小洞里塞入一颗弹珠来把门打开。
22239§booth§buːð§n. 不受干扰的划定空间（如电话亭、投票间等）；售货棚§In our company, we work in separate booths.§在公司里，我们在隔间里工作。
22240§imitation§ˌɪmɪˈteɪʃn§n. 模仿；仿造；仿制品，假货，赝品§A child learns to talk by imitation.§小孩子通过模仿学会说话。
22241§exceed§ɪkˈsiːd§vt. 超过，胜过§World population in the twenty-first century will probably exceed 8 billion.§世界人口总数在21世纪有可能超过80亿。
22242§cohesion§kəʊˈhiːʒn§n. 结合，团结；凝聚力§The Women's Social and Political Union （WSPU） brought the suffragette movement the cohesion and focus it had previously lacked.§妇女社会政治同盟为妇女参政运动带来了前所未有的凝聚力。
22243§livestock§ˈlaɪvstɒk§n. 〈总称〉家畜，牲畜§The country banned the import of all ruminant livestock from Europe.§该国禁止从欧洲进口任何反刍类家畜。
22244§astound§əˈstaʊnd§vt. 使震惊§The eruption in May 1980 of Mount St. Helens, Washington State, astounded the world with its violence.§1980年5月，位于华盛顿的圣海伦斯火山喷发所产生的强大破坏力震惊了世界。
22245§absorb§əbˈsɔːb§vt. 吸收；吸引…的注意，使全神贯注；把…并入，同化§Trees can absorb carbon dioxide.§树木可以吸收二氧化碳。
22246§decrease§dɪˈkriːs§v. 减少，减小[ˈdiːkriːs] n. 减少；减少量§Do you think the cinema has increased or decreased in popularity in recent years?§你认为近年来电影受欢迎的程度是提高了还是降低了？
22247§moral§ˈmɒrəl§adj. 道德的，伦理的 n. [pl.] 品行，道德；寓意，教训§Altering our genetic inheritance is a moral problem.§改变我们的遗传基因是一个伦理问题。
22248§weigh§weɪ§v. 称重；认真考虑，权衡§These boxes are heavy with honey and may weigh up to 90 pounds each.§这些装满蜂蜜的盒子非常重，每个都可能重达90磅。
22249§ceramic§səˈræmɪk§adj. 陶器的；陶瓷的 n. [pl.] 陶瓷器§Glass ceramics can serve as nose cones of missiles.§玻璃瓷可用来制造导弹的头锥体。
22250§acquisition§ˌækwɪˈzɪʃn§n. 取得；获得物§Tom's newest acquisition is a luxurious sports car.§汤姆新获得了一辆豪华跑车。
22251§character§ˈkærəktə(r)§n. 性格，品质；性质，特性；人物，角色；（书写或印刷）符号，文字§The interview does give you a bit of information about an applicant's character.§面试确实能给你提供一些和应聘者性格有关的信息。
22252§arrange§əˈreɪndʒ§v. 安排；排列§The Language Institute activities coordinator can assist students to arrange any sport and leisure activities.§语言学院的活动负责人可以帮助学生安排任何体育和休闲活动。
22253§conservation§ˌkɒnsəˈveɪʃn§n. 保存；保护§We just set up a new wildlife conservation programme here.§我们刚刚在这里启动了一个新的野生动物保护项目。
22254§earthworm§ˈɜːθwɜːm§n. 蚯蚓§The digested dung in these burrows is an excellent food supply for the earthworms.§这些洞里（蜣螂）消化过的粪球给蚯蚓提供了极好的食物来源。
22255§entice§ɪnˈtaɪs§vt. 怂恿，引诱§With the festivals coming, supermarkets begin to push out all sorts of tricks to entice customers to consumption.§随着节日的来临，超市使出各种各样的手段吸引顾客消费。

22256§manipulative§məˈnɪpjələtɪv§adj. 善于操纵的，会摆布人的；熟练操作的，有操作能力的§To handle with negative experiences, a child learns manipulative techniques that are hard to refrain later in life or even become set patterns.§为了应对这些负面体验，儿童学会了控制自己和他人，这种操纵技巧在日后的生活中很难被戒除，甚至会变成既定的行为模式。

22257§memorise§ˈmeməraɪz§vt. 记住，熟记§Before sailing to the sea, prudent navigators will study the sailing directions, and memorise lighthouse locations to prepare themselves for any conditions they might encounter.§出海前，细心的航海员会研究航海说明并记住灯塔的位置，为他们可能会遇到的任何情况做准备。

22258§retrenchment§rɪˈtrentʃmənt§n. 节省；削减§Macro-control and retrenchment curbed sizable speculation venture capital in real estate, leading to the reduction of housing market demand.§宏观调控和费用削减抑制了大量房地产风险投资，致使住房市场需求有所减少。

22259§motivational§ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃənl§adj. 动机的，有关动机的§The science-and-engineering students have motivational, cognitive and emotional barriers in English learning, according to a survey released by the Ministry of Education.§据教育部公布的一项调查结果显示，理工科学生在英语学习中存在着动机、认知和情感方面的障碍。
22260§reinforcement§ˌriːɪnˈfɔːsmənt§n. 增援；加强，加固§The Red Cross blasted the authorities' response to the disaster, making an urgent plea for reinforcements and aid.§红十字会严厉抨击当局对灾难的反应，并紧急呼吁要求增援和救助。
22261§intervention§ˌɪntəˈvenʃn§n. 干涉，干预，介入§In decade, more and more governments strengthened health intervention, and introduced a series of new health-care system.§十年间，越来越多的政府加强对保健的干预，引入了一些新的医疗体系。
22262§infirmity§ɪnˈfɜːməti§n. 虚弱，衰弱§Pathogen infections are among the leading causes of infirmity and mortality among humans and animals in the world.§病原体感染是世界上导致人和动物衰弱和死亡的主要原因之一。
22263§glossy§ˈglɒsi§adj. 有光泽的，光滑的§Out of sudden, the sun broke through from the heavy clouds, shining on her glossy hair, giving it a metallic luster.§突然间，太阳冲破阴云，照在她光滑的头发上，给头发镀上了一层金属的光泽。
22264§escalate§ˈeskəleɪt§v. （使）逐步增长或发展，（使）逐步升级§Instigated by a small number of people with ulterior motives, the demon-stration quickly escalated into a riot.§在少数别有用心的人的煽动教唆下，游行示威很快升级演变成了一场暴动。
22265§extravagance§ɪkˈstrævəgəns§n. 奢侈，挥霍；放肆的言行§He lived in extravagance far beyond his means, which brought his career to a premature end and led to bankruptcy.§他过着超出他收入能力的奢侈生活，从而过早结束了自己的职业生涯，走向破产。

22266§victimise§ˈvɪktɪmaɪz§vt. 使受害，迫害§The World Health Organization reported that environmentally related diseases victimise the most of Africa continent, followed by parts of Southeast Asia.§世界卫生组织称，与环境相关的疾病危害着非洲大陆的绝大部分地区，其次是东南亚的部分地区。
22267§evaluation§ɪˌvæljuˈeɪʃn§n. 估价，评价，评估§Employees should make a copy of their completed Self Evaluation Form for their supervisor in advance of the review meeting.§开评审会之前，雇员应该复印一份填好的自我评估表交给主管。
22268§maternal§məˈtɜːnl§adj. 母亲的；母系的§Susan's maternal grandmother is still alive.§苏珊的外祖母还健在。
22269§crusade§kruːˈseɪd§n. 十字军（远征）；斗争，运动 vi. 加入十字军，投身正义运动§He made it his crusade to teach children to love books.§他把教育孩子热爱书籍作为自己的奋斗目标。

22270§recalcitrant§rɪˈkælsɪtrənt§adj. 顽抗的，反抗的，不服从指挥的§When someone is recalcitrant, he might resist following orders, or going along, even too stubborn to deal with.§如果一个人很桀骜不驯，他可能拒绝服从命令或者与他人合作，甚至固执到无法应付的地步。
22271§mortality§mɔːˈtæləti§n. 死亡率§Although infant mortality varies by ethnicity, deaths among infants with birth defects are similar in all groups.§尽管婴儿的死亡率因种族而不同，但是因出生缺陷而导致的儿童死亡在各个群体中却是类似的。
22272§taunt§tɔːnt§vt. 嘲笑，讥笑 n. [常pl.] 嘲弄的言语，讥讽§People used to tease and taunt him with his cowardice.§过去人们常嘲讽他的胆小怕事。
22273§disseminate§dɪˈsemɪneɪt§vt. 散布，传播§University libraries should aim at disseminating popular culture as well as leading the dissemination of the mainstream culture.§大学图书馆应传播大众文化，还要引导主流文化的传播。

22274§sanction§ˈsæŋkʃn§vt. 批准，认可 n. 批准，认可；约束因素，约束力；[常pl.] 国际制裁§The economic sanctions have long been imposed on the nation due to refusing to sign multilateral agreement.§由于拒绝签署多边协议，长久以来，这个国家一直遭受着经济制裁。
22275§invert§ɪnˈvɜːt§v. （使）倒转，（使）颠倒§Should the image formed on the retina be inverted ?§在视网膜上形成的图像应该是颠倒的吗？
22276§unfortunately§ʌnˈfɔːtʃənətli§adv. 不幸地§Unfortunately, they cannot come to our party.§很遗憾，他们不能来参加我们的聚会了。

22277§frustration§frʌˈstreɪʃn§n. 沮丧，不满§However, you have to admit that you need him so much when the moment of sadness, fear or an acute sense of frustration descends.§但你不得不承认的是，当悲伤、痛苦或是极度沮丧的时候，你如此需要他。
22278§recipe§ˈresəpi§n. 食谱；方法，秘诀，秘方§Errors in the genetic recipe for haemoglobin give rise to the most common single-gene disorder in the world.§血红蛋白中遗传密码出现问题会导致世界上最常见的单基因病变。
22279§condense§kənˈdens§v. （使）压缩，精简；（使）凝结§This article has been adapted and condensed from the article by William and Slater.§这篇文章改编自威廉姆和斯莱特的文章，并进行了精简。

22280§gather§ˈgæðə(r)§v. 聚集，集合，聚拢；收集，采集；逐渐增加；猜想，推测§In the beginning of a new semester, all the new students will gather in the playground to meet the principal and the rest of the faculty.§新学期伊始，所有的新生在操场上集合与校长和其他老师见面。
22281§advertise§ˈædvətaɪz§v. 为…做广告；宣传；（在报刊、电视、广播中）公告，公布§The total number of jobs advertised in the journal was 120.§这本杂志上刊登了120个职位。
22282§utility§juːˈtɪləti§n. 功用，效用；[常pl.] 公用事业§One of many reforms came in the area of public utilities.§众多改革措施中有一条涉及公用事业的变革。
22283§exhibit§ɪgˈzɪbɪt§n. 展览品 v. 陈列，展览；显示§Some of the exhibits at the museum are very precious.§这个博物馆的一些展品非常珍贵。
22284§irrevocable§ɪˈrevəkəbl§adj. 无法取消的，不能改变的§The powers given to these agents are irrevocable.§下放给这些代理商的权力是不可改变的。

22285§shelter§ˈʃeltə(r)§n. 掩蔽（处），隐蔽（处）；住所；保护 v. 掩蔽；躲避§Harbour is a physical concept, a shelter for ships, while port is an economic concept, a centre of land-sea exchange.§Harbour是物质概念，即船的“家”；而port是经济概念，即海陆货物交换的中心。
22286§stock§stɒk§n. 储备品；股票；〈总称〉家畜 vt. 储备 adj. 常备的§Fish stocks here began to decline in the 1950s in South Scotland.§在苏格兰南部，鱼类储量从20世纪50年代开始减少。
22287§devise§dɪˈvaɪz§vt. 设计，发明§Ford devised the first moving auto assembly line.§福特发明了第一条移动的汽车装配线。
22288§career§kəˈrɪə(r)§n. 生涯；经历；职业§The idea of having a single career is becoming old fashioned.§只从事一种职业的想法现在已经开始变得落伍了。
22289§humidity§hjuːˈmɪdəti§n. 湿度；潮湿§The wooden frame warped in the humidity.§木框因受潮而弯曲了。
22290§hollow§ˈhɒləʊ§adj. 中空的，空心的；空洞的；（声音）沉闷的；虚伪的，空虚的 vt. 挖空，凿空§Dung beetles' homes are hollowed out from within.§蜣螂的家是从里面往外挖空的。
22291§statistic§stəˈtɪstɪk§n. 统计数值；[pl.] 统计学§The writer pointed out that the employment statistic was deceptive.§作者指出这个就业统计数据不可信。
22292§bark§bɑːk§vi. 吠叫 n. 犬吠声；树皮声§Our neighbour's dog barks constantly.§邻居家的狗总是叫个不停。
22293§burrow§ˈbʌrəʊ§v. 挖掘；钻进；翻寻 n. 地洞§Most dung beetles burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels.§大多数蜣螂在地下挖洞，并将粪球埋在地下。
22294§equivalent§ɪˈkwɪvələnt§adj. 相等的，等量的 n. 相等物，等价物§At that time, the cost of a bulb was equivalent to half a day's pay for the average worker.§那时，一个灯泡的成本相当于普通工人半天的工资。
22295§fatigue§fəˈtiːg§n. 疲劳，劳累 v. （使）疲劳§Part-time workers are less likely to succumb to fatigue in stressful jobs.§兼职工人在有压力的工作中不太可能被疲劳压垮。
22296§bibliography§ˌbɪbliˈɒgrəfi§n. 参考书目；书目；文献学§I'm looking for those books which my professor lists in the bibliography.§我正在找教授列在参考书目单上的那些书。

22297§probable§ˈprɒbəbl§adj. 很可能的，大概的§It is probable that, some time in the tenth century, gun powder was first compounded from its basic ingredients of saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur.§火药很可能最早在十世纪的某个时间由硝石、木炭和硫磺等基本成分混合而成。
22298§treadmill§ˈtredmɪl§n. （人或畜力的）踏车；单调的例行工作，乏味繁重的工作§I can't get off the office treadmill.§我无法摆脱单调的坐班工作。
22299§flavour§ˈfleɪvə(r)§n. 风味，滋味 vt. 给…调味§Each country's coffee has a different flavour.§各国的咖啡都别具风味。
22300§asymmetry§ˌeɪˈsɪmətri§n. 不对称§Asymmetry is a common feature of the human body.§不对称是人体共同的特点。
22301§lethal§ˈliːθl§adj. 致命的，破坏性的，毁灭性的；有害的§Bugs and weeds become resistant to poisons, so next year's poisons must be more lethal.§臭虫和野草对农药产生了抗药性，所以来年农药的杀伤力就需要再强一些。
22302§stare§steə(r)§vi. 凝视，盯着看 n. 凝视，注视§He stared at the word trying to remember what it meant.§他盯着这个单词，努力想记住它的意思。
22303§colony§ˈkɒləni§n. 殖民地；（动植物的）群体§Different animals in the colony had different manifestations of the disease.§同一群体的不同动物对同一疾病有不同的表现形式。
22304§stab§stæb§v. （用刀等锐器）刺，戳，捅 n. 刺，戳，捅；刺（或戳、捅）的伤口§Such a vicious lie could be nothing but a stab in the back.§这样一种恶毒的谎言简直是暗箭伤人。
22305§fingerprint§ˈfɪŋgəprɪnt§n. 指纹，手印§Systems using fingerprints, hands, voices and faces are already on the market.§市场上已出现了利用指纹、手印、声音和面部进行识别的系统。
22306§enthusiasm§ɪnˈθjuːziæzəm§n. 热情，热心，积极性；热衷的事物§She shows great enthusiasm for the movie.§她对这部电影表现出极大的热情。
